## Microsoft apologizes for email disruption, says AI agents not responsible

“We're collecting enormous amounts of personal health data through phones and wearables, but turning that information into something people can actually understand and act on remains a challenge,” Brownstein said. [...] According to a February 2026 Oxford study published in Nature Medicine, AI chatbots accurately identify medical conditions nearly 95% of the time when tested on clinical cases, yet everyday users reach the right answer less than 35% of the time when trying to understand dense guidance. Yet 35% of adults, or about half of adults under 30, are already using AI chatbots, according to the Pew Research Center. [...] Users will be able to ask the study app everyday health questions and see linked, peer-reviewed clinical citations -- showing users where the advice is coming from.

Apple is collaborating with OpenEvidence, an AI tool that is used by doctors and is trained on sources like medical journals that may not be available to other AI platforms.

Full access to OpenEvidence is currently only available to health care professionals and returns answers in a language that they are used to.

 Galaxy S25 Ultra review – battery life

  I'm glad the Galaxy S Ultra's most predictable spec is finally changing
 Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra Back Panel And Rear Cameras [...] ## TL;DR

 Samsung is redesigning Expert RAW for the Galaxy S27 and One UI 9.5 with a cleaner interface, larger controls, and customizable shortcut buttons.
 The app adds new shooting features including Burst mode, a wider Virtual Aperture range from f/1.4 to f/22, a Tint control, and photo aspect ratio options.
 Early signs also point to future video support, with settings for stabilization and resolution/frame rate visible in this build.
